key_insight: SIM-PINN combines projection-based decoupling, iterative coupling, and multi-stage neural networks to improve convergence and accuracy for incompressible Navier–Stokes equations.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a mesh-free route to incompressible flow simulation while addressing optimization difficulties caused by nonlinear dynamics, coupled constraints, and spectral bias.
method: Separate the Navier–Stokes system into linearized momentum and pressure Poisson equations.
Solve the subproblems with dedicated multi-stage neural networks linked by projection-based inner iterations.
Progressively refine velocity fields at targeted frequencies, recovering the coupled nonlinear solution upon convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved convergence and accuracy on steady lid-driven cavity and unsteady Kolmogorov flow simulations, without quantitative results.
watch_item: Computational cost and scalability beyond the two demonstrated flow cases are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Projection-based segregated, iterative, and multi-stage physics-informed neural network for incompressible Navier-stokes equations
